note: Algorithmic engineering software for 3D printing, Munich. HV entered 2021-01 (Fund VIII) and co-led the $7.8M 'first venture round' (3DPrint.com), which carries no round word. note: Chef-cooked meal delivery (eating.de), Berlin (founded 2015). Founders Fund and Holtzbrinck 'investieren in der Seed-Runde einen Millionenbetrag' (Gruenderszene, Nov 2015). Shut down in Jan 2018 after failing to raise again (deutsche-startups, 2018-01-05), so the row did not graduate. The eatingpoint.be link on HV's archived page is an unrelated Belgian caterer.

Web music-playlist app, Cologne (founded 2011). Musicplayr 'hat eine Seedfinanzierung von Holtzbrinck Ventures erhalten', EUR 500K (press release, 2012-10-22). Musicplayr 24/7 GmbH went into liquidation in Jan 2015 and was deleted in Nov 2016 (North Data); no later round.

Kyte (kyte.com), the 2006 mobile and live video platform, San Francisco. Swisscom, Klaus Hommels and Holtzbrinck Ventures joined in 2007 after a $2.25M first round (GigaOm), with no round word. acq. by KIT digital, Jan 2011 (~$5.7M; KIT digital's 8-K exhibit). The old site's 'decentral.tv / kyte' row is this company. Not the 2021 car-rental startup Kyte.

Berlin company builder (Jan Beckers, founded 2011; HitFox Game Ventures, AppLift, FinLeap, Heartbeat Labs). Holtzbrinck Ventures backed it beside founder money (EU-Startups interview, 2013), with no round word. Renamed IONIQ Group GmbH in May 2019; it still files accounts (2024 accounts filed May 2026) and holds a Finleap stake.

Casual web-games portal fettspielen.de, Karlsruhe, operated by FamilyOne GmbH (later Rumble Media GmbH). Holtzbrinck Ventures and European Founders Fund backed it (deutsche-startups, 2009-01-07), with no round word. The operator went into liquidation on 2018-08-16 and was deleted on 2020-08-26 (North Data); the domain now belongs to an unrelated company.

Online bookshop buecher.de, Augsburg (founded 1999). A corporate-era holding the unit listed under 'Exits' on its 2006 site (D2); entry 1999-09, the round not named. Majority-owned by the Weltbild group by 2014 (Der Spiegel); the Augsburg KG went into insolvency in July 2024 and liquidation in Oct 2024.

Quantum computing software, Berlin (founded in Karlsruhe; the registered seat moved to Berlin in May 2026, HRB 287200 B, per its imprint). HV's entry 2023-12-19 is the EUR 10.5M seed announced that day, led by HV Capital and DTCF (The Quantum Insider).
